skill.name: snowtower-user
skill.description: Guides end users through Snowflake access requests, RSA key setup, connection steps, and basic SnowTower troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Help users request Snowflake access and connect with Snow CLI, Python, or the Snowflake web interface.
skill.author: Database-Tycoon

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many security patterns, but review found they are legitimate documentation examples for Snowflake onboarding. The skill does not contain prompt injection, secret exfiltration, hidden execution, or instructions to share private keys.

remediation.issue: RSA key commands can be sensitive if users misunderstand what to share.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing private-key warning and add a short reminder near the request step to paste only the public key.

remediation.issue: The relative issue-form link may be unclear outside GitHub rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Describe that the access form is a GitHub issue template so users understand the link target.

content.value_statement: New Snowflake users need clear steps for access, keys, and first connections. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through SnowTower onboarding and common fixes.
actual_capabilities: Explains the three-step SnowTower access request flow.
Guides users through RSA public and private key generation for Snowflake.
Shows connection examples for Snow CLI, Python, and the Snowflake web interface.
Describes default roles, warehouses, and personal databases after approval.
Provides troubleshooting steps for authentication, privileges, and warehouse state.
limitations: Does not approve access or modify Snowflake permissions.
Requires users to follow their organization’s GitHub issue workflow.
Uses placeholder account, role, and warehouse names that must be replaced.
Does not validate local key files or network connectivity automatically.

use_cases.title: Onboard a new analyst
use_cases.description: Walk a new data analyst through key generation, access request submission, and first Snowflake login.

use_cases.title: Connect a script to Snowflake
use_cases.description: Help an engineer choose RSA key authentication and configure Snow CLI or Python connector settings.

use_cases.title: Resolve first-login issues
use_cases.description: Guide a user through common Snowflake authentication, role, privilege, and warehouse troubleshooting steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start my Snowflake access request
prompt_templates.prompt: I need Snowflake access through SnowTower. Walk me through what I need to do before I submit the request.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and submit my public key
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me generate the RSA key pair for Snowflake and identify exactly which public key text I should include in my access request.

prompt_templates.title: Connect after approval
prompt_templates.prompt: My SnowTower access was approved. Show me how to connect with Snow CLI and verify my current user, role, and warehouse.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot authentication and privileges
prompt_templates.prompt: I cannot connect to Snowflake or I get insufficient privileges. Help me diagnose key permissions, account settings, role selection, and access gaps.

output_examples.input: How do I request Snowflake access?
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the three-step flow: generate RSA keys locally, submit the GitHub access request with the public key, then connect after approval.

output_examples.input: Authentication failed when I used Snow CLI.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks approval status, account identifier, username, private key path, key permissions, and whether the submitted public key matches.

output_examples.input: What should I do after my account is approved?
output_examples.output: The assistant describes using the assigned username, account identifier, default role, and warehouse, then running first-session Snowflake checks.

best_practices: Paste only the public key into access requests, never the private key.
Replace every placeholder account, role, warehouse, and username before connecting.
Start with a simple current-user query before running larger workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not share the private RSA key in tickets, chat, or prompts.
Do not use the web UI password for scripts or automated jobs.
Do not request broad data access without a clear business justification.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for analysts, data scientists, engineers, and new team members who need SnowTower Snowflake access.

faq.question: Does this skill grant Snowflake access?
faq.answer: No. It explains the request process, but an administrator must review and approve access.

faq.question: Which key should I share in the access request?
faq.answer: Share only the public key. Never share the private key or paste it into a ticket.

faq.question: Can it help with Snow CLI setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides Snow CLI connection steps and a basic query to test the connection.

faq.question: Can it help with Python connections?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows the connector fields needed for account, user, key file, warehouse, and role.

faq.question: What if I need more database access later?
faq.answer: Open a new access request and include the exact databases, schemas, roles, and business reason.
